headline: Kim Jong Nate Played A Perfect Lineup. It Scored 81.54.
kicker: (100.0 percent efficiency, 2-11 in all-play, 0-2. Four of his bench players did not play.)
lede: Nathan made every correct decision available to him and scored 81.54, because the decisions available to him were Austin Ekeler, Trevor Etienne and Brian Thomas Jr., all three picked up this week, all three started, 4.96 points between them. His bench was four players who did not play and an empty slot. First 0-2 week of his season. The median fell to 113.97, the lowest line of the year, 24.63 below last week's. Greg (Miley) cleared it by 2.35 and Andrew missed it by 2.35, with Caleb Williams' 16.5 on his bench. Nishil made nine adds and still left his IDP slot empty. Jon finally started the right quarterback and scored the league low anyway. Chris benched a 26.96 quarterback and is 12-0. Barrett scored 170.18 and is 11-1. Abhishek played a perfect lineup too, and his was worth 164.80.

sections.awards: Fourteen citations. Three perfect lineups this week, and they finished 2-0, 2-0 and 0-2.
sections.power: Season to date: record, points, all-play and this week's form, weighted, with movement from last week. Best lineup is the record each team would own if it had started its best legal lineup every week, everyone else exactly as they played. The tax is the difference: wins left on your own bench.
sections.median: Week 6's line was 113.97, the lowest of the season, a week after the highest. Greg (Miley) made it by 2.35. Andrew missed it by 2.35 with a better quarterback on his bench. Greg (IR) lost his game by 45.80 and got a win here anyway; Tom won his game with 95.16 and lost here by 18.81. Right of the line is a win.
sections.standings: Week 6 scoring, both results, and how much of your own roster you managed to start. Efficiency is what you scored over what your best legal lineup would have scored. Injured reserve does not count against you. Players who did not play do not either, which is how 81.54 rates as perfect.
sections.bench: 126.46 points of lineup regret this week, down from 129.24. Andrew and Nishil account for 43.68 of it. Leo the Cleo benched the best quarterback on his own roster and nobody could punish him for it.
sections.faab: Every dollar of Week 6, audited. $70 spent, 40 adds. Germie Bernard ($21) returned 20.2. Chris Godwin ($21) returned 5.7 from the bench. Michael Pittman ($3) went straight to IR. Nishil made nine of the 40 adds.
sections.money: Auction dollars against everything each player has scored so far, started or not. A.J. Brown: $45, 8.3 points in six weeks, 4.2 of them this week from IR.
sections.studs: The best and worst starts of Week 6, measured against what Yahoo thought they would do. Bijan Robinson cost $69 and finished with minus eight receiving yards.
sections.games: The long version, closest game first.

games.note: The closest game of the week, and nobody in it played well. Nathan scored 81.54 with a perfect lineup: Judkins, Tyler Warren, Ollie Gordon and Justin Jefferson, none of whom played, and one roster spot empty. So he started what he bought. Austin Ekeler, a Saturday free agent, 1.7. Trevor Etienne, a Sunday free agent, 3.26. Brian Thomas Jr., claimed for $0 after Jon cut him, 0.00 at flex, a week after scoring 1.0 for Jon from one solo tackle. Brandon Aubrey kicked one extra point: 1.0. Kenyon Sadiq started again: 1.7. Tom scored 95.16 and won by 13.62 with Derrick Henry ($45) at 4.5 and Tyler Higbee, a Sunday pickup, at 2.2 in the flex. Tom missed the median by 18.81, 3-10 in all-play, and is 10-2 on a five-game head-to-head streak. The house does not need to be good. It needs you to be worse.

Maclane's $41 receiver finally paid: Keon Coleman, 13.9 and a touchdown. Then he started KaVontae Turpin at flex for 1.0, the same Turpin who sat on ShakeNBake's bench in Week 1 and returned 194 yards against him in Week 4. Rico Dowdle scored 6.4 on the bench. Cameron Dicker made 53 yards of field goals for 5.3. None of it mattered, because Will is 2-10. Will finally started Matthew Stafford, after benching his 383 yards last week: 16.88. Then he did the receiver thing in reverse. Week 5: Romeo Doubs started for 2.1, Terry McLaurin (10.2) and Denzel Boston (12.62) on the bench. Week 6: McLaurin started for 3.2, Boston for 2.0, Doubs on the bench for 10.7. Will is not unlucky. He is perfectly wrong, on a one-week delay. 0-2, four straight losses, best-lineup record 7-5.

Darrius went 2-0 and still left 39.5 points on his bench: Alvin Kamara 13.9, Stefon Diggs 13.4, Keenan Allen 12.2, while Michael Wilson (5.2) and Parker Washington (8.68) started. Keenan Allen has now been benched for 7.0 and 12.2 in back-to-back weeks. Darrius has the third-most points in the league, a 10-2 best-lineup record, a 6-6 real one and the worst luck index in the league at -1.92. Anuj got 24.2 from Tre Tucker and 13.8 from Hunter Henry, a Thursday free agent, and lost by 32.10 anyway. He started Emmett Johnson at flex (5.4) with Jerry Jeudy (8.9) on the bench. Six straight head-to-head losses. 0-6 against actual teams, 1-5 against a number. 1-11.

Barrett scored 170.18, the high score of the week, 13-0 in all-play, 98.7 percent efficient. Brian Robinson went back to the bench and scored 2.56 there, the first correct Brian Robinson decision of the season. Kenneth Walker 27.9. Chiefs, $4 on waivers, 15.74. He also paid $3 for Michael Pittman and sent him straight to IR, and $12 for Kimani Vidal to bench him. 11-1, 6-0 against the median, best-lineup record 12-0. Greg (IR) lost by 45.80 and still went 1-1, because 124.38 was 10.41 above the lowest median of the season. Germie Bernard, $21 on waivers, started and scored 20.2: the best FAAB dollar of the week. Blake Corum scored 13.0 on his bench, a week after scoring 14.7 on his bench. Juwan Johnson started at tight end for 0.00. 33 moves.

Greg (Miley) played a perfect lineup for the second straight week. Last week it was because his whole bench was on bye. This week Cam Skattebo ($21) scored 0.00 at running back and the lineup was still perfect, because nobody on the bench could have replaced him. Trey Smack, picked up at 12:21 on Sunday, kicked for 11.8. Travis Hunter scored 19.9 in the IDP slot by catching a touchdown. 116.32, cleared the median by 2.35. Jon started Deshaun Watson, a Wednesday free agent, over Bo Nix: 9.46 to 4.48. After two straight weeks of benching the wrong quarterback, Jon got one right. He scored 68.94, the league low, 0-13 in all-play. Bijan Robinson ($69) scored 6.3 with minus eight receiving yards. Michael Mayer scored 14.0 on the bench while Rashod Bateman started at flex for 0.00. Chris Godwin, $21 on waivers, benched, 5.7. T.J. Watt scored 1.0, an improvement on last week.

Chris benched Tyler Shough, who threw three touchdowns and ran one in for 26.96, and started Josh Allen, 18.30. Wrong by 8.66. He also had Jahmyr Gibbs on bye. He won by 50.12. Malik Nabers 25.5, the Saints, a Wednesday free agent, 17.62. 12-0, six straight, $95 of FAAB untouched. Nishil scored 75.04, 1-12 in all-play. He made nine adds this week and did not put anybody in his IDP slot. It sat empty all Sunday. He picked up Najee Harris at 9:11 on Sunday morning and started him: 0.20, on two rushing yards. Roschon Johnson, picked up Wednesday, scored 13.5 on the bench. Nishil is 1-11, 0-6 against the median, and has made 30 moves to get there.

Abhishek played a perfect lineup: 164.80, 100.0 percent, 12-1 in all-play, beaten only by Barrett. Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdowns for 28.34, the best start of the week. Jaylin Noel, projected for 5.99, scored 22.38 at flex. Carnell Tate, 1.1 at flex last week, scored 16.0. The 49ers and Evan Williams, both Wednesday free agents, both started. He also picked up Jordan Addison at 9:15 on Sunday morning, with the Vikings on bye. Andrew missed the median by 2.35 and Caleb Williams scored 16.5 on his bench while Dak Prescott started for 13.02. The quarterback alone clears the median. Kyle Pitts caught two touchdowns on the bench for 20.5 while Harold Fannin started at tight end for 1.4. Last week: Pitts 12.7 on the bench, Fannin 0.9 starting. 24.68 points of regret, the most in the league for the second straight week.
